context: Normalize path comparison in the tests (or emit native paths from the script); make the signal-trap test skip or assert correctly where bash signal semantics differ on Windows runners.
description: Nightly integration-smoke (windows-latest, 3.12) fails tests/integration/worktree/test_worktree_claim_benchbox_scratch.py (2 tests): asserts 'WORKTREE_PATH=C:\Users\...' but the claim script emits '/c/Users/...' (MSYS form under Git Bash). Also test_worktree_claim_signal_exit.py::test_worktree_claim_int_trap_exits_nonzero_after_cleanup fails ('assert 0 != 0' — INT trap exits 0 on Windows). Pre-existing before the agent-instruction PRs; discovered 2026-07-29.

preserves.behavior: POSIX behavior of worktree claim scripts unchanged

verifications.expected: all pass; Windows proof via next nightly

work_units.evidence: The recipe prints whatever its own shell considers the path to be; on Windows that shell is Git Bash/MSYS, which renders C:\\Users\\... as /c/Users/.... The assertion compared that against Path.resolve()'s native spelling, so it failed on spelling alone. Replaced the substring check with an exact comparison on a canonical form: normalize_path() lowercases and translates a leading /X/ drive segment, but ONLY when os.name == 'nt' - on POSIX a leading single-letter segment like /a/b is an ordinary directory and must not be rewritten. emitted_worktree_path() additionally asserts exactly one WORKTREE_PATH= line, so this is strictly stronger than the substring test it replaces. Verified both branches by exercising normalize_path directly against the literal strings from the nightly log: emitted '/c/Users/runneradmin/AppData/.../BenchBox.pool-01' and native 'C:\\Users\\runneradmin\\AppData\\...\\BenchBox.pool-01' now compare equal under os.name='nt', while under posix '/a/b/c' is untouched and case is preserved. Locally 4 passed.
work_units.summary: Normalize WORKTREE_PATH assertion for MSYS vs native path forms

work_units.evidence: Platform-gated rather than 'fixed', because the test is POSIX-only by construction and the behaviour it exercises does not exist on Windows. It shims git with an extensionless '#!/bin/sh' script placed first on PATH, but Windows resolves git.exe/git.cmd and never executes an extensionless file, so the shim is bypassed entirely; it then drives the recipe's INT trap with 'kill -INT $PPID', which has no Windows equivalent. The nightly evidence matches exactly: returncode 0 with stderr "Switched to a new branch 'feature/signal-test'" - the real git ran, the claim succeeded, and there was no interrupt to trap, so 'assert result.returncode != 0' failed as 'assert 0 != 0'. Added pytest.mark.skipif(os.name == 'nt') to the module pytestmark with that reasoning as the skip reason. POSIX behaviour is untouched: the test still runs and passes on macOS/Linux (4 passed locally), and no script under _project/scripts was modified.
work_units.summary: Fix or platform-gate the INT-trap exit-code test
